description.value: This study investigated whether semantic deficits in dementia are associated with abnormal eating habits and preferences, using voxel-based morphometry and diffusion tensor imaging.

spans.text: We used voxel-based morphometry and diffusion tensor imaging to identify regions and white matter tracts of significant atrophy associated with the performance at the semantic tasks and the pathological scores at the APEHQ.

description.value: A cross-sectional observational study of patients with behavioural frontotemporal dementia, semantic variant of primary progressive aphasia, Alzheimer's disease, and healthy controls.

spans.text: We enrolled seven patients with behavioural frontotemporal dementia (bvFTD), five patients with the semantic variant of primary progressive aphasia (svPPA), and 11 patients with Alzheimer’s disease, as well as 21 healthy controls (HC).

name.value: Correlation between left anterior cingulum volume and eating habits scores

definition.value: The volume of the left anterior cingulum was significantly correlated to both semantic deficits and eating disorders.

spans.text: Interestingly, correlation analyses revealed that the volume of the left anterior cingulum was significantly correlated to both semantic deficits and eating disorders.

spans.text: We know that this tract is involved in language (see for instance Forkel et al., 2014) and we also found a significant positive correlation between the right anterior segment of the arcuate and semantic performance and a negative correlation with the pathological scores at all of the APEHQ subscales.
Finally, we ran Spearman’s correlations between pathological scores at the subscales of the APEHQ and participants’ scores at our semantic tasks and the volume of white matter tracts of interest.
